text: Embers in the Southern Hills

Jieyang is yours, and the warlords of the south have noticed. They will not come at you all at once - they will send one commander, to see what you are, and what they learn from him is what the rest will believe. So do not merely hold the town. Take a warband back up into the hills, fall upon him where the trees grow close, and let the survivors carry word of it home. One broken column is worth a hundred sermons.
[[i]]Defeat the marked enemy commander in battle. Fighting from the hills gives your men the advantage.[[/i]]
The Yellow Sky Is Not Yet Fallen

The Great Teacher is dead, his brothers with him, and the great host that once shook the empire is scattered into a hundred bands of hungry men. What survives of the Way survives in fragments - a rite half-remembered here, a passage copied badly there. Gather the scholars who still keep the old texts and set them to work on the first of the reforms. If the Yellow Sky is to rise again in the south it must first be remembered correctly, and the faithful have a way of carrying strange old things down out of the hills once they hear the words spoken properly again.
[[i]]Open the reforms panel and complete any reform.[[/i]]
Voices Among the Faithful

There is more will in these hills than there are men to direct it. Villagers who have hidden bandits, hunters who know every deer path on the ridge, headmen who have quietly refused the tax collector for years - each of them commands the trust of a valley, and trust is the only currency worth anything out here. Find one such voice and bind them to your cause. A leader the people already follow costs you nothing to make.
[[i]]Recruit a new character to serve your faction.[[/i]]
The Faithful Gather

Word of the ambush has run ahead of you. Men are coming down out of the hills with billhooks and mattocks and their grandfathers' spears, asking whether the Yellow Sky has truly returned to the south. Do not turn them away for want of arms - arm them. A host that comes to you willingly will hold when a paid one runs.
[[i]]Recruit units until your armies number at least thirty in total.[[/i]]
Jieyang Under the Yellow Sky

Begin where the ground is softest. Jieyang is a market town, not a fortress - a place where the rice of the whole delta is weighed and taxed and carried away, and where the people doing the weighing have grown very tired of who it is carried away to. Take it, and take it first, before the south works out what you intend. A movement that lives in the hills is a rumour; a movement that holds a market town is a government. There will be an officer in the gatehouse worth stripping, besides.
[[i]]Conquer Jieyang. Left-click your army, then right-click the settlement to attack.[[/i]]
Raise Something From the Ashes

The Han built and the Han burned, and what they left the bandits picked over. Your people have grown so used to hiding that they have forgotten how to make. Begin the work: a granary, a barracks, a smithy - it hardly matters which, so long as they see a thing raised by their own hands that no magistrate will come to take. Faith is easier to keep under a roof.
[[i]]Select a settlement and construct a building in one of its slots.[[/i]]
A Name Whispered Beyond Tongan

In Luoyang they do not know your name. In the villages three valleys over they are beginning to. That is the only reputation that has ever mattered to the Yellow Turbans - not titles granted from above, but the slow accumulation of people who would rather answer to you than to the magistrate. Grow it. The empire will notice you soon enough, and it would be better to be noticed as a power than as a nuisance.
[[i]]Gain {{tr:faction_progression_prestige}} by taking territory and winning battles to advance your faction rank.[[/i]]
The South Learns to Fear the Turban

The prefects of the southern commanderies have begun writing to one another about you. Their letters are still contemptuous - a bandit, an upstart, a peasant with delusions - but they are writing, and men who write about you are men who are afraid of you. Give them more to write about.
Shelter the Ember

The rites cannot be kept in the open. Every gathering under the sky is a gathering some informer can report, and there are still magistrates in the south who will burn a village for a single yellow cloth. Build the shrine where the hills close over it - a hidden place where the ember can be tended out of the wind. What is sheltered can be fed. What is fed can be made to spread.
[[i]]Construct the Hidden Shrine in one of your settlements.[[/i]]
Every Hand Willing

There are more volunteers than there is work assigned to them, and idle faith curdles into grievance faster than any commander likes to admit. Set your officers to the task of employing them - in the fields, in the forges, on the roads that only your people know. A movement is held together by the work it gives its believers.
[[i]]Assign a character to the Employ Volunteers assignment.[[/i]]
A Host Out of the Hills

What began as a warband is becoming an army, and an army must be large enough that no single defeat unmakes it. Draw in the bands still hiding in the southern forests, the deserters, the debt-broken, the ones with nothing left to lose. They have all been waiting for someone to give their anger a shape.
Three Provinces, One Sky

One province can be surrounded. Three cannot be taken in a single season. Push out from Tongan until the Yellow Sky covers ground deep enough that no warlord can reach your shrines without first fighting through your people. Depth is the only mercy the south has ever offered.
Warlord of the Southern Marches

You are no longer a rebel to be hunted; you are a neighbour to be reckoned with, and the difference is measured entirely in how many men will answer your call. The great families of the south send envoys now instead of soldiers. Keep growing, and the envoys will start bringing gifts.
The Rites Restored

Piece by recovered piece, the Way is becoming whole again in the south. What your scholars have assembled is not quite what the Great Teacher taught - some of it is older, some of it is newly made - but it is coherent, it is written down, and it can be taught to a village in a single evening. That is more than the Han can say of their classics.
Sanctuary of the Southern Spark

The hidden shrine has outgrown its hiding place. Pilgrims come now from beyond your borders, and a shrine that cannot hold its own pilgrims is a shrine that will be trampled by them. Raise it into a true sanctuary - stone where there was timber, courtyards where there were footpaths. Let the south have a place it can point to and say: there, that is where it burns.
[[i]]Upgrade your shrine to the Sanctuary of the Southern Spark.[[/i]]
The Faithful Are Legion

There was a time when you counted your men by name. That time is gone. Muster a host large enough to hold every valley you have taken and still march on another - the Yellow Sky has never survived by standing still.
Five Provinces, One Sky

Five provinces is no longer a rebellion. It is a state, whether or not anyone in Luoyang is willing to write the word down. Take them, and govern them well enough that the people never wish to be governed otherwise.
The Ember Becomes a Blaze

What you sheltered in a hillside shrine is now burning across half the south. Warlords who once ignored you now shape their campaigns around you. There is no longer any path back to the hills - only forward, and the men who follow you know it as well as you do.
Paths Only We Know

Your people have spent a generation moving through this country without being seen, and that knowledge is worth more than any general's map. Set it down properly: the deer paths, the fords that hold in flood, the ridges where a column can lie all day within a bowshot of the road and never be found. Let the enemy have the highways. We will have everything else.
Men of the Forest

There are hunters in the southern woods who have never sworn to anyone and never needed to - men who can put an arrow through a boar at fifty paces and be three valleys away before the beaters arrive. They will not stand in a shield wall and they should not be asked to. Take them as they are, and send them where no line of battle could ever go.
[[i]]Recruit three units of Men of the Forest.[[/i]]
Eight Provinces, One Sky

Eight provinces, and the shrines in every one of them. The south is no longer somewhere the Yellow Sky is remembered - it is somewhere the Yellow Sky rules. Finish what the Great Teacher began here, and then look north.
Crowned Beneath a Yellow Sky

The old titles were always meaningless - conferred by an emperor who could not feed his own capital, on men who had never worked a day of their lives. Take the highest of them anyway. Not because it means anything, but because the people who once used it to look down on your kind should have to watch you wear it.
The Yellow Sky Ascendant

The final teachings are recovered, reconciled and set down. What the Great Teacher held in his own head is now written in a hundred hands across a hundred shrines, and no army in the world can burn it out of them all. Whatever happens to you, the Way will outlive the Han.
Twelve Provinces, One Sky

Twelve provinces. Every one of them was somebody's before it was yours, and every one of them is quieter and better fed now than it was under the men who lost it. Let that be the argument. Let it be the only argument that has ever been needed.
The Inferno of the Yellow Sky

It began as a hidden shrine in a hillside where the trees grew close enough to hide the smoke. Raise it now to its final form - a sanctuary so vast that the fires on its terraces can be seen from the far side of the province on a clear night, and no man in the south need ask any longer whether the Yellow Sky has returned. The ember you carried out of Tongan is an inferno. Let it be seen.
[[i]]Upgrade your shrine to the Inferno of the Yellow Sky, its final form.[[/i]]
The Renegades of Tongan

Wu Huan came out of the southern hills with a warband and a half-remembered creed. Build that into a power the empire cannot ignore - grow your faction until the warlords of the south must treat with you as an equal.
The Yellow Sky Over All

The Han mandate is exhausted; something must take its place, and every warlord in the empire intends it to be theirs. Rise above them all. Let the Yellow Sky be the sky that everyone under heaven stands beneath.
Let No Rival Sky Remain

So long as one rival claimant lives, the empire has somewhere else to look. Destroy every warlord who still styles themselves the leader of the world, and leave the people no throne to hope for but yours.
Heaven Made Whole

There is no north and no south, no Han and no rebel - only the land, and the people who work it. Bring all of it beneath the Yellow Sky, and let the age of magistrates and tax farmers end where it began: in the fields.
